issues.claim: "1.5–3.0 staff on exceptions today" (section 2) and "3–6 staff in client service" (section 3)
issues.problem: No cited source gives functional headcount. PDR publishes only total headcount ('more than 300 full-time associates' on About, 'over 250' on Our Staff) and a list of job titles. The two ranges are inferences from those titles but read as current facts inside the 'Expected impact' brackets. Section 2 partly hedges with the 'Worth checking together' line; section 3 has no hedge at all.
issues.fix: Add a short qualifier, e.g. '(we estimate 1.5–3.0 staff-equivalents from your published roles) ' and for section 3 '(3–6 by our estimate from your published roles)'. Keeps the numbers but stops them reading as known facts.

issues.claim: "Orders arrive from 30+ platforms into Microsoft Dynamics, with Order Desk handling multi-channel edits and fulfilment rules"
issues.problem: Slight conflation of two separate statements. The technology page says PDR integrates with over 30 front-end platforms and uses Microsoft Dynamics 'to manage each client's business'; it does not say orders flow from those platforms into Dynamics. The e-commerce page separately credits Order Desk with automation 'to edit orders, management fulfillment' for multiple selling channels - 'fulfilment rules' is a paraphrase. Not contradicted, but the flow as described is not stated anywhere.
issues.fix: Reword to what is published: 'You integrate 30+ front-end platforms with Microsoft Dynamics, with Order Desk on top for multi-channel order edits and fulfillment automation; Toronto runs the same systems.'

issues.problem: The body (title through the 'Prepared from publicly available information' line, excluding the 'For the founder' block) runs about 470 words, above the ~450-word target for this format.
issues.fix: The wage clause '(customer service rep median, NJ, 2025, x1.25 for benefits)' is repeated verbatim in all three impact lines. State it once in section 1 and use 'at the same $28.68/hour loaded rate' in sections 2 and 3 - saves roughly 26 words and brings the body to ~445.

issues.claim: "x1.25 for benefits" applied to the BLS median
issues.problem: The multiplier is an internal assumption; no source is given for it. It is not inflationary (BLS employer-cost data puts benefits at roughly 30% of total compensation, i.e. a ~1.4x load), so the direction is safe, but it is presented as a defined input without being labelled.
issues.fix: Either cite the BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation series for the load, or write 'we load 25% for benefits (a conservative assumption)'.

issues.claim: "your pricing page sends new enquiries to an Excel questionnaire at info@" (founder email) and "emailed to info@" (audit intro)
issues.problem: Not a factual error - the address on the site is info@pdrnj.com - but the shorthand 'info@' is imprecise and reads as sloppy in an email written to the CEO, and 'still a downloaded Excel questionnaire' carries a mild note of judgement.
issues.fix: Use the full address once (info@pdrnj.com) and then 'your pricing inbox'; drop 'still' so the sentence states the process without implying PDR has been slow to change.
